            CRYPTOGRAPHIC DEEP DIVE
            
Why Custom Salted SHA-256 Beats Predefined SHA256 on Primary Keys

            

              Enterprise primary keys follow predictable formats such as 'CUST-1001'..'CUST-9999' or sequential integers. When masked with predefined SHA256, an analyst can compute TO_BASE64(SHA256('CUST-1001')) in a CTE and join it against the masked column to de-anonymize every customer record in milliseconds.
            

            

              The Solution — Custom Masking Routine (Priority #1):
              By creating a GoogleSQL UDF with OPTIONS (data_governance_type = 'DATA_MASKING') that concatenates an enterprise secret pepper inside the routine body, analysts with maskedReader can still join customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id because both columns evaluate to the exact same deterministic salted digest, yet dictionary attacks fail completely.
            

            
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.data_policies_example.fn_salted_sha256`(val STRING)
RETURNS STRING
OPTIONS (data_governance_type = 'DATA_MASKING') AS (
  CAST(SHA256(CONCAT(val, 'REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_ENTERPRISE_SECRET_PEPPER_2026')) AS STRING FORMAT 'HEX')
);

            

              
            

          


          

            RELATIONAL ANTI-PATTERN ALERT
            
Why ALWAYS_NULL Must Be Used Instead of DEFAULT_MASKING_VALUE on Join Keys

            

              For external auditors or restricted roles that should not join tables on customer_id, choosing between ALWAYS_NULL and DEFAULT_MASKING_VALUE is critical:
            

            
    
              
  • 
                ALWAYS_NULL on customer_id (Safe Join Blocker):
                Replaces every PK and FK with NULL. In SQL three-valued logic, NULL = NULL evaluates to UNKNOWN, so customers JOIN orders ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id safely returns 0 rows.
              
    • 
              
  • 
                DEFAULT_MASKING_VALUE on Secondary PII/Financial Columns (Safe Value Scrubber):
                Replaces STRING columns (email, phone, tax_id) with "" and numeric columns (credit_limit_usd) with 0.0 so single-table queries remain type-compatible without null-pointer failures.
              
    • 
              
  • 
                DEFAULT_MASKING_VALUE on a Join Key (Dangerous Anti-Pattern):
                If applied to customer_id (`dp-persona-defaultpk`), every customer PK becomes "" and every order FK becomes "". Since "" = "" is TRUE, an 8-row customer table joined with a 12-row order table explodes into 96 corrupted rows (8 × 12 Cartesian product)!
              
    •
